tagline: Valley farms and bluestone country connect two historic railroad viaducts.
intro: Viaduct Valley Way runs between Lanesboro and Dixon in Pennsylvania’s Endless Mountains, through valley farmland and bluestone quarry country. VisitPA presents the 37.3-mile scenic byway as a drive linking historic villages and two railroad viaducts, Starrucca and Tunkhannock. On PA 92, woodland alternates with fields, and the road winds beside Tunkhannock Creek into Nicholson. The road passes beneath the Tunkhannock Viaduct, carrying Norfolk Southern’s Sunbury Line over both the highway and the creek.

The byway designation came in stages, beginning with sections of PA 92 in 2005. In 2007, the Dixon-to-Lanesboro designation brought PA 92, PA 171 and two other state routes into the named journey. Another PA 92 segment in Oakland Township followed in 2012. The bridges tell an older transportation story: Starrucca crossed a valley that the railroad had considered filling with an embankment. Tunkhannock belonged to a cutoff replacing a winding, hilly rail route.

Begin at Starrucca near Lanesboro. Susquehanna Depot brings the journey to the Susquehanna River. Southward, PA 92 links Jackson, South Gibson and Lenox through woods and farmland. Nicholson brings the concrete viaduct overhead. Beyond it, the creek-side road passes Starkville and East Lemon before reaching Dixon and US 6.

moments.title: Starrucca Viaduct
moments.text: Starrucca’s stone arches answer a problem of width: the railroad abandoned a proposed embankment across the valley as impractical. The New York and Erie Railroad built the crossing in 1847–48, using locally quarried bluestone, brick interior walls and concrete pier bases. Eight hundred workers completed it in a year. The original broad-gauge track gave way to two standard-gauge tracks in 1886, and concrete reinforced the deck in 1958. The viaduct remains in railroad use. At completion in 1848, it was the world’s largest stone railway viaduct, spanning Starrucca Creek near Lanesboro.

moments.title: Susquehanna Depot
moments.text: Susquehanna Depot made locomotives as well as receiving trains. The railroad established workshops here while building its line through the county in 1848. The workforce eventually exceeded 1,000, and the complex included a 33-stall roundhouse, foundry and rail yard. By 1887, the shops produced five locomotives a month. The Susquehanna station, opened in 1865, included a large hotel called Starrucca House. The locomotive shops moved to Hornell in 1928. The roundhouse closed in 1952 as Erie changed from steam to diesel. Most shop buildings were demolished in 1980 and 1981.

moments.title: Tunkhannock Viaduct
moments.text: At Nicholson, PA 92 passes beneath the Tunkhannock Viaduct. Almost half the bridge’s bulk lies underground. Above the creek bed, it rises 240 feet; measured from bedrock, its height reaches 300 feet. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad opened it in 1915. It formed part of the Nicholson Cutoff, which shortened the rail journey by 3.6 miles and saved an hour for freight trains. Construction began in May 1912 with excavation for all 11 piers, reaching bedrock as much as 138 feet below ground. The concrete bridge still carries regular through freight daily.
